text: {Elihu Begins His Discourse} d "Now please listen to what I have to say, Job. Listen to every word!
Look! I've begun to speak, {Lit. I've opened my mouth} and I'm fashioning my words. {Lit. and my tongue speaks in my mouth}
I speak from the innocence {Or integrity} of my heart; and my lips will utter what I sincerely know.
"The spirit of God fashioned me; and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me, if you can! Present your case! Take your stand in my presence!
Look! As far as God is concerned, {Lit. Look! Before God} I'm just like you are I, too, have been pinched off from a piece of clay.
Don't be afraid of me; I'll go easy {Lit. my hand won't be heavy} on you."
{Elihu Reviews Job's Claim for Innocence} d "You spoke clearly so I could hear; I've heard what you've said:
«I'm pure. I'm without sin; I'm innocent. I'm harboring no iniquity inside of me.
Nevertheless, God {Lit. he} has found a pretext to attack me; he considers me his enemy.
He has bound my feet in shackles, and keeps watching everything I do.»" {Lit. watching all my paths}
{God Responds to Humanity's Need} d "You aren't right about this; My response is that God is greater than human beings.
Why are you arguing with him? He doesn't have to give explanations for what he does to you!
"God speaks time and time again {Lit. speaks once and twice} but nobody notices
in a dream or night vision, when a deep sleep falls on mankind while they sleep on their beds.
That's when he opens the ear of mankind, authenticating his messages {Lit. mankind, sealing his instruction} to them,
turning a person from his actions, keeping him {Lit. man} from pride,
sparing his soul from the Pit {I.e. the realm of punishment in the afterlife} and his life from violent death. {Lit. from death by the sword}
"Job {Lit. He} is being reproved by painful bed rest, with continuous aching in his bones.
He cannot stand his food, and he {Lit. his soul} has no desire for appetizing food.
His flesh wastes away; his bones, which once couldn't be seen, are visible.
His soul is getting close to the Pit; {I.e. the realm of punishment in the afterlife} his life is approaching its executioner."
{God Delivers through His Ransom} d "If there's a messenger {Or an angel} appointed to mediate for Job {Lit. him} one out of a thousand to represent the man's integrity on his behalf,
to show favor to him and to plead, «Deliver him from having to go down to the Pit {I.e. the realm of punishment in the afterlife} I know where his ransom is!'
Let his flesh be rejuvenated {Lit. grew fresh} as he was in his youth! Let him recover the strength of his youth.
Let him pray to God and he will accept him; he will appear before him with joyful shouts!"
{The Song of the Ransomed} d "He'll sing to mankind with these words: «I've sinned. I have twisted what is right. Yet he has not repaid me like I deserve. {The Heb. lacks like I deserve}
He has redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit; {I.e. the realm of punishment in the afterlife} my life will see the light.'
Indeed God does all these things again and again {Lit. things twice, three times} with a person
to bring back his soul from the Pit; {I.e. the realm of punishment in the afterlife} to light him with the light of life."
{Elihu Invites Job to Respond} d "Job, pay attention! Listen to me! Be silent and let me speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak up, because I'd be happy to vindicate you.
But if you have nothing to say, then at least listen to me! Be quiet and learn some wisdom from me."
